images.title: A credit adds to the balance
images.purpose: Show that a credit of 60 put into an account holding 100 makes a balance of 160.
images.composition: One wide bar centred with a bracket below it, wide margins around.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal bar made of exactly 8 equal squares in a row: the first 5 filled teal #0072B2 (balance 100), the last 3 filled amber #E69F00 (credit 60). A single bracket under the whole bar spans all 8 squares. Exactly 1 bar, 2 colours, 1 bracket.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a gap between the teal and amber squares
images.takeaway: A credit is money put in, so it adds to the balance.
images.description: A bar of 8 equal squares, 5 teal for the balance of 100 and 3 amber for the credit of 60, with a bracket under all 8 showing 160.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the money already there, then the credit added, then the total.

image_decisions.why: Adding a credit to a balance is a picture idea; one clean bar carries it.
